report:
### Efficacy of Hypnosis for Smoking Cessation

The scientific evidence on whether hypnosis helps with smoking cessation is **mixed and inconclusive**. While hypnosis may benefit certain individuals, high-level research does not establish it as superior to other standard quit methods.

#### Evidence Supporting Hypnosis
Some clinical trials report positive results, particularly when combined with other interventions. For instance, a randomized controlled trial found that hypnosis combined with nicotine patches resulted in higher abstinence rates than standard counseling with patches (https://web.archive.org/web/20220303055959/https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18569754/). The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) acknowledges that hypnosis is widely studied and used in integrative health settings for smoking cessation (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/hypnosis).

#### Evidence Showing Inconclusive or Weak Benefit
Major systematic reviews find limited evidence for hypnosis as a standalone treatment. The Cochrane Systematic Review concluded there is insufficient high-quality evidence to show whether hypnotherapy is more effective for smoking cessation than other behavioral supports or unassisted quitting (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31198991/). Additionally, a 2023 meta-analytic overview in *Frontiers in Psychology* noted that effect sizes for hypnosis in smoking cessation vary widely across reviews and are frequently non-significant (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238/full).

### Conclusion
Hypnosis may serve as a helpful complementary tool for some smokers, but strong scientific proof of its independent efficacy remains lacking compared to first-line, evidence-based treatments like behavioral counseling and nicotine replacement therapy.
